q-160619:
Consider the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors. Computing the images of $\{i,j\}$ under $A$, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =A(i)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i \\ {j}^{′} & =A(j)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033087/assets/9fae3ec0ada3008937d88e4e76374a56da4369b1821cfee072c90d88b562df46.png)

So, the matrix represents a rotation of $\pi $ radians (counterclockwise or clockwise) about the origin.

Therefore, in order to find $Av$, we need to rotate $v$ (counterclockwise or clockwise) by an angle of $\pi $ radians, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033087/assets/ae800b271848948b5f60f5cd7c1cecd163c2aa7399e9a87e2a52d158857c6a42.png)

q-160627:
Consider the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors. Computing the images of $\{i,j\}$ under $A$, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =Ai=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j \\ {j}^{′} & =Aj=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033087/assets/77936c4115b37d79ae301a93b218ecd23114ae4ad42d8298b8f058c1f50e82a2.png)

So, the matrix represents a rotation of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians **clockwise** about the origin.

Therefore, in order to find $Av$, we need to rotate $v$ **clockwise** by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033087/assets/d5ff1c1a7c99b08d04d2ac58d9f8195ee29c8b564873a9abfb2635e93cec1968.png)
